text: The Prophet, peace be upon him, passed away in the year 632. More than six hundred years later, a people arrived at Baghdad who fit his description.
In Sahih al-Bukhari, he describes a people with small eyes, red faces and flat noses, faces like shields covered in leather. In another narration, they wear shoes made of hair.
A report in Abu Dawud adds a great city on the Tigris, with a bridge. Some scholars understand it as Baghdad, which was founded in 762, over a century after he died.
In 1258, the Mongols under Hülegü took Baghdad and ended Abbasid rule there.
The objection is that the Arabs already knew the Turks. But the claim is not one detail. It is the whole picture: the appearance, the attack, and a city not yet built.
Weigh it as a whole, and check the sources yourself before you cite it.
